# Purpose and scope

This assessment decides which process parameters of the A-Mab drug substance process are
characterized, and what kind of study each one receives. It is performed before any
characterization study is executed, so it draws on prior knowledge, the platform history and
the process description alone. Its output is a scope. For every parameter carried in the
process description it records the quality attribute that the parameter could put at risk,
an initial risk priority number, and the study type assigned to it.

The assessment does not classify parameters. Classification into critical, well controlled
critical, key and general process parameters is an outcome of the studies, and it is
recorded in the characterization reports PCR-003 through PCR-010. The assessment also
defines no operating range and no design space, and it states only what must be studied and
why.

The scope is the drug substance train described in PTP-001, which runs from the production
bioreactor to ultrafiltration and diafiltration. That train has `{python} f"{n_steps}"` unit
operations and `{python} f"{ra['n']}"` process parameters, and it must control
`{python} f"{rc['n_cqa']}"` drug substance quality attributes, all of which are carried into
the assessment. Vial thaw and seed expansion are not included, and neither are the drug
product operations. Analytical methods, raw materials and facility systems are qualified
under their own procedures and fall outside an assessment of process parameters.

PTP-001 is the parent of this document (@tbl-related), and the scope defined here is
consolidated across the campaign in PCMP-001 before it is instantiated step by step in the
characterization plans PCP-003 through PCP-010. Each plan sets the ranges to be studied and
the acceptance criteria for its own step. A plan that departs from the scope assigned here
records the reason for the departure.

# Risk assessment methodology

Two decisions are taken in this document and they draw on different parts of the A-Mab
method [@amab2009]. Parameters are ranked on the severity, occurrence and detection scales
of the case study, which the case study applies after characterization and which are applied
here prospectively, at a point in development where no characterization data exist. The
study type assigned to each parameter follows the case study's risk ranking and filtering
rule, and that rule is given in §2.4. Each parameter receives three scores. Severity comes
from the quality attribute that the parameter could affect, occurrence describes how likely
an effect on that attribute is thought to be, and detection describes whether the controls
that exist today would find the failure, and how late. The product of the three is the risk
priority number (RPN), and parameters are ranked on it.

## Severity

Severity is a property of the quality attribute and not of the parameter, so a parameter is
scored at the severity of the most severe attribute it could affect, and a parameter that
could move high mannose sits at the top of the scale even where the movement expected is
small. The scale runs from a deviation with no product quality consequence to one that would
cause a batch to be rejected (@tbl-sev-scale). The priority band in the step tables of §4
follows the severity alone. A parameter linked to an attribute of severity
`{python} f"{sev_high_band}"` or above takes the High band, a parameter linked to a less
severe attribute takes the Medium band, and a parameter that reaches no attribute takes the
Low band.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_scale_df("severity"))
```

: Severity scale for the effect of a parameter excursion. {#tbl-sev-scale}

## Occurrence and detection before characterization

Occurrence and detection are scored by convention in this assessment, because neither can be
measured before the studies are run. A parameter that is linked to a quality attribute is
given the occurrence score for an effect that is credible but not yet quantified. A
parameter that affects only process performance is given a lower score, since the platform
history for such parameters is long and an excursion costs performance without putting an
attribute at risk.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_scale_df("occurrence"))
```

: Occurrence scale for a parameter excursion. {#tbl-occ-scale}

The scale in @tbl-occ-scale is the case study scale and it counts how often an excursion
happens. Occurrence carries a different meaning here. It stands for the likelihood that an
excursion moves the attribute, which is the quantity the characterization studies are run to
settle, so a parameter linked to a quality attribute is scored between the Moderate and High
bands of the scale, and a parameter that affects only process performance is scored at the
Low band.

Detection follows the control that exists today (in-process monitoring, in-process testing
and release testing), and the scale is given in @tbl-det-scale. A parameter that could
reduce viral clearance receives the worst detection score, because clearance is not measured
on a routine batch and its loss would not appear in release testing.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_scale_df("detection"))
```

: Detection scale for the resulting failure. {#tbl-det-scale}

The three conventions, and the number of parameters each one covers, are given in
@tbl-init-rule. The classes are mutually exclusive, so the counts in the last column sum to
the `{python} f"{ra['n']}"` parameters in the assessment, of which viral safety accounts for
`{python} f"{rc['n_viral_params']}"`.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_initial_score_rule_df())
```

: Pre-characterization occurrence and detection scores by parameter class. {#tbl-init-rule}

## Criticality and parameter risk are separate

Two assessments meet in this document and they are not the same thing. The criticality of a
quality attribute is scored on impact and uncertainty, which is Tool #1 of the case study,
and it produces a continuum of criticality rather than a division into critical and not
critical [@amab2009; @ichq9]. Attribute criticality is a property of the molecule and of
what the attribute does in the patient, whereas the risk of a process parameter is scored on
severity, occurrence and detection and is a property of the process and of how well that
process is currently understood. An attribute of very high criticality does not make every
parameter that touches it a high risk parameter, and a parameter can score high because the
process cannot yet detect the failure, even where the attribute itself is moderate.

## The study type decision

Two things decide the study type, and the initial RPN is not one of them (@tbl-study-rule).
The first is whether an excursion in the parameter could reach a quality attribute. The
second is whether the effect of the parameter is expected to depend on the other parameters
at the same step. A parameter that meets both is carried into the designed experiment for
its unit operation, so that its effect is estimated alongside the other parameters at that
step and alongside the interactions between them. A parameter that is linked to an attribute
but whose effect is expected to be independent is studied on its own, and the reason is
stated with the assignment. A parameter that affects only process performance is also
studied on its own, unless it is a principal driver of a response that the designed
experiment at its step already measures, in which case it is carried as a factor of that
design. The rule allows a parameter to be left unstudied as well, and that outcome requires
prior knowledge that the parameter reaches no attribute and that the range given in the
process description is already justified. No parameter in this assessment met both
requirements, and the count is given in the table.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_study_rule_df())
```

: Study-type decision rule and the number of parameters reaching each outcome. {#tbl-study-rule}

## What this assessment does not produce

Three outputs lie outside this assessment by design: it does not estimate the size of an
effect, it does not resolve the interactions between parameters, and it sets no proven
acceptable range. It also produces no residual risk number, and a residual assessment needs
the characterization results and the control strategy that follows from them, so it is
performed after the studies report and is consolidated in PCMR-001.

# Quality attributes at risk

The severity axis of this assessment comes from the drug substance quality attribute
register, which is reproduced in @tbl-cqa. The register carries `{python} f"{rc['n_cqa']}"`
attributes, of which `{python} f"{rc['n_critical']}"` carry a high or very high criticality
designation. Criticality and severity appear as separate columns because they answer
separate questions: criticality states how much the attribute matters to the patient and how
certain that judgement is, and severity states what would happen to a batch if the attribute
moved outside its acceptance range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.cqa_table())
```

: Drug substance quality attributes, their acceptance criteria, criticality and severity. {#tbl-cqa}

The top of the severity scale holds `{python} f"{rc['n_cqa_sev_max']}"` attributes. High
mannose carries the highest Tool #1 score in the register and is formed in the culture. The
two viral clearance attributes are expressed as a cumulative log reduction across the whole
process, so their acceptance criteria are a floor and not a window. A batch that fails
either of them cannot be brought back by reprocessing, and that is what puts both at the top
of the scale.

Afucosylation is scored high because the mechanism of action of A-Mab is antibody dependent
cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC) and afucosylation moves that activity. Galactosylation is
scored high on a different activity, since the case study reports a correlation between
galactose content and complement dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) across the whole
galactosylation range [@amab2009]. Both are formed in the production bioreactor. Prior
knowledge from the platform indicates that neither is modified by the purification train, so
the culture parameters carry the whole of the risk for them and no downstream step can
correct an excursion.

The process impurities behave differently, since host cell protein (HCP), residual DNA and
leached Protein A are reduced at more than one step and no single unit operation carries the
whole risk for any of them. The same holds for the two viral clearance attributes, and the
two are built differently. The enveloped virus claim takes independent contributions from
the low pH hold, the anion exchange step and the virus filter. The parvovirus claim rests on
the anion exchange step and the virus filter alone, because a low pH hold does not
inactivate a virus without an envelope. Cross step credit is part of the assessment for
these attributes, so a parameter is scored on the attribute it puts at risk and the report
for each contributing step states how much of the attribute that step delivers.

The production bioreactor sets `{python} f"{n_bioreactor_cqas}"` of the
`{python} f"{rc['n_cqa']}"` attributes, and the remaining `{python} f"{n_other_cqas}"` are
set at the capture step, the low pH hold and the anion exchange step (@tbl-cqa). That
distribution is the main reason the bioreactor carries the largest parameter set in this
assessment.

# Parameter risk ranking by unit operation

The parameter level outcome is given step by step below, and @tbl-step-overview gives its
shape: the number of parameters each step carries, how many of them are linked to a quality
attribute, the split between multivariate and univariate study, and the highest initial RPN
reached at the step.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_step_overview_df())
```

: Parameters carried, study split and highest initial RPN, by unit operation. {#tbl-step-overview}

The highest initial RPN in the assessment is reached at
`{python} f"{n_steps_at_rpn_max}"` steps, and all of them are viral steps. That number is
shared by `{python} f"{rc['n_at_rpn_max']}"` parameters, and it is the product of the top
severity, the pre-characterization occurrence convention and the worst detection score.
`{python} f"{rc['n_steps_no_cqa']}"` steps, harvest and UF/DF, carry no parameter linked to
a quality attribute at all, and both are assessed on process performance alone. The
bioreactor sits below the viral steps on initial RPN and above every other step on parameter
count.

Each step below carries two tables. The first ranks the parameters of the step and gives the
three scores behind the ranking. The second records the prospective failure mode and its
effect. Where a failure mode quotes a range or a limit, that value is taken from the process
description, and none of it is an outcome of a characterization study.

## Production bioreactor (Step 3)

The bioreactor carries more parameters than any other step, and it is where the glycan,
charge variant, aggregate and impurity attributes are formed. It carries
`{python} f"{ov.loc[3, 'Parameters']}"` parameters, of which
`{python} f"{ov.loc[3, 'CQA-linked']}"` are linked to a quality attribute (@tbl-risk-bio).
Culture pH reaches the highest initial RPN at the step because it is the only bioreactor
parameter that could move high mannose, which is the one attribute the step forms that sits
at the top of the severity scale. Culture temperature, dissolved carbon dioxide (pCO₂),
osmolality and culture duration are scored one severity band lower, on the attributes each
of them reaches.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("bioreactor"))
```

: Production bioreactor parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-bio}

The prospective failure modes are given in @tbl-fm-bio, and they act by two different
mechanisms. A pH or temperature excursion acts on the glycosylation machinery directly, and
the effect is expected to be continuous across the range. Culture duration acts indirectly,
because an extended culture is harvested at lower viability, which raises host cell protein
and DNA in the harvest and can raise aggregate as well. Separating a direct effect from an
indirect one, and separating both from the interactions between the parameters carried into
the design, is what the designed experiment at this step is for.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("bioreactor"))
```

: Production bioreactor prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-bio}

Dissolved oxygen, initial viable cell concentration, basal medium concentration and nutrient
feed volume are scored on process performance. They drive titre and culture consistency
(peak cell density, integral of viable cells, final titre), and no product quality effect is
expected for them over the ranges the process uses. Basal medium concentration is a partial
exception, because prior product knowledge records a statistically significant but shallow
effect of medium concentration on afucosylation, and that effect is too small to move the
attribute within its acceptance range, so the parameter is carried on process performance
and studied on its own.

## Harvest and clarification (Step 4)

Harvest forms no quality attribute and is credited with no clearance, and the
`{python} f"{ov.loc[4, 'Parameters']}"` parameters it carries govern clarification
efficiency and filter capacity, each of them scoring `{python} f"{rc['rpn_min']}"`, the
lowest initial RPN in the assessment (@tbl-risk-harvest). The recorded failure modes are
losses of yield or of filter capacity (@tbl-fm-harvest). Feed quality to the capture step is
bounded by the post clarification turbidity range in the process description, which runs
from `{python} f"{turb_prange}"` with a normal operating range of
`{python} f"{turb_nor}"`. Turbidity is an in-process limit and not an operator set point,
and it is carried here because it bounds the material the capture step receives.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("harvest"))
```

: Harvest and clarification parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-harvest}

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("harvest"))
```

: Harvest and clarification prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-harvest}

## Protein A chromatography (Step 5)

Protein A capture sets leached Protein A and removes the bulk of the host cell protein and
DNA load that enters the purification train. The largest further reductions come later, at
cation exchange for host cell protein and at anion exchange for DNA. The step carries
`{python} f"{ov.loc[5, 'Parameters']}"` parameters, of which
`{python} f"{ov.loc[5, 'CQA-linked']}"` are linked to a quality attribute, and both of
those are linked to host cell protein (@tbl-risk-proteina). Protein load and elution buffer
pH reach the same initial RPN, and the failure modes recorded for them share a mechanism.
Both increase the amount of host cell protein that leaves the step with the product, and the
assessment expects the two to interact (@tbl-fm-proteina).

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("protein_a"))
```

: Protein A chromatography parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-proteina}

Load flow rate and end of pool collect carry no attribute risk. Both are taken into the
designed experiment even so, because step yield is measured on the same runs and these are
the two parameters that move it. Operating temperature and bed height carry no specific
failure mode, and the generic entry recorded against them states the position the assessment
takes. No significant product quality impact is expected from either of them, even for an
excursion beyond the range proposed for characterization, and a univariate study is enough
to support that range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("protein_a"))
```

: Protein A chromatography prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-proteina}

## Low-pH viral inactivation (Step 6)

The low pH hold reaches the highest initial RPN in the assessment, and it does so on
`{python} f"{ov.loc[6, 'CQA-linked']}"` of its `{python} f"{ov.loc[6, 'Parameters']}"`
parameters (@tbl-risk-vi). The step sets the cumulative clearance of enveloped virus
(XMuLV), which is an attribute at the top of the severity scale that no in-process test can
measure, and inactivation pH, hold time and temperature are all scored there.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("viral_inactivation"))
```

: Low-pH viral inactivation parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-vi}

Inactivation pH is the sharpest case in the assessment, because it carries a failure mode in
both directions. Too high a pH leaves the inactivation incomplete, and too low a pH risks
aggregation and precipitation of the product (@tbl-fm-vi). The two failure modes act on
different attributes and bound the acceptable range from both sides, which is why the
parameter is taken into a designed experiment together with hold time and temperature.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("viral_inactivation"))
```

: Low-pH viral inactivation prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-vi}

A-Mab concentration in the hold is scored on process performance. No effect on inactivation
kinetics, aggregation or charge variants is expected over the concentration range the step
sees, and the parameter is assigned a univariate study.

## Cation exchange chromatography (Step 7)

Cation exchange is the principal aggregate polishing step and a major clearance step for
host cell protein, DNA and leached Protein A. It carries
`{python} f"{ov.loc[7, 'Parameters']}"` parameters, of which
`{python} f"{ov.loc[7, 'CQA-linked']}"` are linked to a quality attribute (@tbl-risk-cex).
Protein load, elution buffer pH and elution stop collect are scored on aggregate and reach
the highest initial RPN at the step, while load and wash conductivity is scored on host cell
protein, one severity band lower.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("cex"))
```

: Cation exchange chromatography parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-cex}

The failure modes at this step are all reductions in separation quality (@tbl-fm-cex),
because a high load and an extended stop collect both bring more of the aggregate peak into
the pool, and elution pH moves where the aggregate elutes relative to the monomer. The
assessment expects load, elution pH and wash conductivity to interact, which is why
`{python} f"{ov.loc[7, 'Multivariate']}"` parameters go into one designed experiment.
Elution flow rate affects peak shape and yield and is studied on its own.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("cex"))
```

: Cation exchange chromatography prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-cex}

## Anion exchange chromatography (Step 8)

Anion exchange and small virus retentive filtration are the two steps at which every
parameter carried is linked to a quality attribute, and anion exchange is the larger of the
two (@tbl-risk-aex). It is the last chromatographic step in the train, it sets the
cumulative clearance of parvovirus (MVM), and it also contributes to enveloped virus
clearance and to host cell protein removal. Load pH, load conductivity and operating flow
rate are scored on viral clearance and reach the highest initial RPN in the assessment,
while equilibration and wash conductivity and protein load are scored on host cell protein.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("aex"))
```

: Anion exchange chromatography parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-aex}

Operating flow rate is the one parameter in the assessment that reaches the highest initial
RPN and is still not assigned to a designed experiment. The reason is mechanistic. Flow rate
is expected to act through residence time, and not through the ionic conditions that govern how
impurities and virus bind to the resin, so its effect should not interact with load pH or
with conductivity. The recorded failure mode is a loss of clearance margin at high flow
(@tbl-fm-aex). The parameter is assigned a justified univariate study, and PCP-008 records
that justification together with the range it studies. If the univariate result does not
support the expectation, the parameter returns to the multivariate scope.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("aex"))
```

: Anion exchange chromatography prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-aex}

## Small-virus retentive filtration (Step 9)

Virus filtration carries `{python} f"{ov.loc[9, 'Parameters']}"` parameters and both are
linked to viral clearance (@tbl-risk-vf). The step provides the dedicated size based removal
of small virus and is the principal contributor to the parvovirus claim, so both parameters
reach the highest initial RPN in the assessment. Filtration volume is the parameter the
parvovirus claim is most sensitive to. Prior knowledge for this filter type indicates that
the log reduction for parvovirus falls as the volumetric load rises, and the failure mode
recorded against it is breakthrough above the control limit (@tbl-fm-vf). Filtration
pressure is scored with it, because pressure and load act together on the filter.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("virus_filtration"))
```

: Small-virus retentive filtration parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-vf}

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("virus_filtration"))
```

: Small-virus retentive filtration prospective failure modes and effects. {#tbl-fm-vf}

## Ultrafiltration and diafiltration (Step 10)

Ultrafiltration and diafiltration concentrates the product and exchanges it into the
formulation buffer, and the step forms no quality attribute and is credited with no
clearance, so all `{python} f"{ov.loc[10, 'Parameters']}"` of its parameters score
`{python} f"{rc['rpn_min']}"` (@tbl-risk-ufdf). The recorded failure modes are incomplete
buffer exchange, a loss of flux and a final concentration outside the drug substance
specification (@tbl-fm-ufdf), and all three parameters are assessed univariately.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_score_table("ufdf"))
```

: Ultrafiltration and diafiltration parameter risk ranking. {#tbl-risk-ufdf}

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_mode_table("ufdf"))
```

# Characterization study assignment

The assessment assigns a study to every parameter it carries:
`{python} f"{ra['n_multivariate']}"` parameters go into a multivariate designed experiment,
`{python} f"{ra['n_just_uni']}"` is assigned a justified univariate study, and
`{python} f"{n_plain_univariate}"` are assessed univariately on process performance. No
parameter was filtered out as too low a risk to study. The parameter list contains only
settings and in-process limits that the operator controls, and each of those is given at
least the univariate work needed to justify its range.

```{python}
#| output: asis
show(RC.ra_assignment_df())
```

: Characterization scope handed to each plan, by unit operation. {#tbl-assign}

The assignment by step is given in @tbl-assign. A designed experiment is carried at
`{python} f"{ra['n_doe_steps']}"` of the `{python} f"{n_steps}"` steps. Harvest and UF/DF do
not, because no parameter at either is linked to a quality attribute, and a multivariate
design would resolve interactions with no quality consequence.

The multivariate group is the larger one and it is defined by attribute risk, with two
additions at the capture step. A parameter enters the designed experiment for its step when
an excursion could move an attribute and when its effect is expected to depend on the other
parameters at that step. Load, pH and conductivity at the chromatography steps are the
clearest example of that general case. Each of them changes the chemical environment in
which the product and the impurities bind, so their effects cannot be estimated one by one
and then added together. The two additions are load flow rate and end of pool collect at the
capture step, which reach no attribute and are carried because step yield is measured on the
same runs.

The univariate group divides into two, and `{python} f"{n_plain_univariate}"` parameters
affect process performance alone, for which a univariate study establishes the range over
which the performance measures (titre, yield, filter capacity) stay acceptable. The anion
exchange operating flow rate is the only parameter linked to a quality attribute that is
assigned a univariate study, and its justification is mechanistic and is given in the anion
exchange section above.

This assignment is prospective, and it is bounded in three ways. It rests on prior knowledge
of the platform and of the three antibodies made on it before A-Mab, so it assumes that
platform behaviour transfers. It fixes a study type but not a range. Each plan sets the
ranges to be studied, and a range wider than the routine control range is what makes the
study informative [@amab2009]. The assignment is also revisited when the studies report. A
parameter that turns out to carry no effect keeps its place in the knowledge space as
evidence of robustness, and a parameter that interacts more strongly than expected can be
returned to a multivariate design in a later study.

# Assumptions and limitations

The assessment assumes that the platform transfers, since A-Mab is made on the humanized
IgG1 platform used for the three earlier products (X-Mab, Y-Mab and Z-Mab), and the failure
modes recorded here are the platform's failure modes. Where the mechanism at a step is the
platform mechanism, that assumption is strong. Where A-Mab differs from the earlier
products, it is weaker, and the characterization studies are the check on it.

The parameter list is assumed to be complete. It holds the operating parameters named in the
process description, and it does not hold material attributes, resin and membrane life
cycle, or equipment design, all of which are controlled by other means. Leached Protein A is
the clearest case. The register assigns that attribute to the capture step, and no operating
parameter in the list is linked to it, because the amount that leaches is governed by the
resin and by its sanitization history under SOP-2008. An assessment of operating parameters
cannot cover an attribute of that kind, and the capture study measures it as a step response
instead (PCP-005).

Occurrence and detection are conventions here and not measurements, and they are applied
uniformly to whole classes of parameter, so the risk priority number ranks parameters
against each other and does not measure risk on an absolute scale. Comparison of the number
between two parameters is meaningful. Comparison of the number against an external threshold
is not.

Severity is taken from the most severe attribute a parameter can affect, and nothing in the
score rewards a parameter for affecting several attributes at once. Culture pH and culture
duration show the limit of that convention. Each of them is linked to
`{python} f"{n_attr_max_param}"` attributes, and both still score below the viral
parameters, which are linked to one or two. The ranking should be read with that in mind.
The study assignment does not depend on it, because both parameters enter a designed
experiment on either reading.

The assessment cannot know effect sizes or interactions. It can only say where they are
plausible. Every quantitative statement about the effect of a parameter on an attribute
belongs to the characterization reports, and nothing in this document should be read as one.

# Outputs and downstream use

This assessment produces one output: the study type assigned to each process parameter, with
the attribute risk that justifies it. PCMP-001 consolidates the assignment across the
campaign and fixes the common scale down and statistical approach. Each plan from PCP-003 to
PCP-010 takes the share belonging to its own step, sets the ranges and states the acceptance
criteria, and each report from PCR-003 to PCR-010 records the outcome and classifies the
parameters of that step. PCMR-001 consolidates the classifications and the resulting control
strategy, and the whole package is listed in @tbl-package.

```{python}
#| output: asis
print(corpus_docs_md(DOC))
```

: The A-Mab drug substance document package. {#tbl-package}

The assessment is re-executed when the process description changes, when a parameter is
added to a step, or when a characterization study returns a result that the assessment did
not anticipate. A re-execution is recorded as a new version of this document and is
referenced by the plans it affects.

This assessment is approved by the functions listed in the approval record at the front of
the document (@tbl-appr). Approval by Quality Assurance releases the scope defined here for
use in PCMP-001 and in the characterization plans PCP-003 through PCP-010.
